smell_elimination.justification: The refactoring only renames methods without addressing the core interface segregation violation. All four abstract methods remain in DataWithCoords, still forcing DataArray to implement multi-variable methods and Dataset to implement single-variable methods. The fat interface is unchanged, just cosmetically renamed. No evidence that CoordinateTransformable Protocol, strategy registry system, or forced implementations in DataArray/Dataset were removed or simplified.

cross_file_coordination.justification: The diff only shows changes to common.py (base class). No changes shown to DataArray/Dataset implementations, CoordinateTransformable Protocol in types.py, or strategy registry in ops.py. Since the method signatures changed (_resolve_multi_var_coord_state → _get_coord_state, _validate_single_var_bounds → _validate_var_bounds), this would break all implementations unless they were updated elsewhere, but no such updates are visible in the diff.

structural_soundness.justification: Renaming methods doesn't fix the structural problem of a fat interface. The same four abstract methods exist with the same forced implementation requirements. The cosmetic name changes (_get_coord_state, _validate_var_bounds) make the methods sound more general but don't address the fundamental issue that single-variable and multi-variable concerns are bundled in one interface. If anything, the more generic names hide rather than clarify the segregation violation.

code_quality.justification: The new names (_get_coord_state, _validate_var_bounds) are slightly more generic and the updated docstrings attempt to make the methods sound applicable to all cases. However, this superficial generalization obscures the problem rather than solving it. The documentation now tries to justify why one method handles both single and multi-variable cases ("validates each independently or a specific variable"), which papers over the segregation issue. The code remains readable but doesn't improve maintainability.

interface_decomposition.justification: No interface decomposition occurred. The four abstract methods remain bundled in DataWithCoords with the same requirement that all subclasses implement all methods. The only change is cosmetic renaming, which doesn't split the interface along responsibility boundaries. DataArray still must implement multi-variable coordination (_get_coord_state from multi-var's _resolve_multi_var_coord_state) and Dataset still must implement single-variable validation (_validate_var_bounds from _validate_single_var_bounds).

split_quality.justification: No splitting was performed. The same four methods remain abstract and required. The renaming to more generic names (_get_coord_state, _validate_var_bounds) actually makes it harder to see that these serve different roles (multi-var coordination vs single-var validation), thus making the segregation violation less obvious rather than fixing it. All unnecessary stubs that DataArray and Dataset had to implement still exist, just under different names.

interface_segregation_restoration.justification: The interface segregation violation is completely unaddressed. All four abstract methods remain in DataWithCoords, forcing all subclasses to implement all methods. The renaming from _resolve_multi_var_coord_state to _get_coord_state and _validate_single_var_bounds to _validate_var_bounds doesn't change the fact that DataArray must implement methods for multi-variable coordination and Dataset must implement methods for single-variable validation. The more generic names arguably make the violation worse by hiding the conceptual mismatch behind vague terminology.

strategy_dispatch_simplification.justification: No changes visible to the strategy registry system. The diff only shows base class method renaming. The complex machinery of register_coord_strategy decorator, _coord_operation_strategies dict, resolve_coord_operation dispatch, _compute_coord_alignment_key(), and the two strategy implementations (_multi_var_coord_strategy, _single_var_coord_strategy) remain entirely unchanged. If the method names changed in the base class, the strategy implementations calling these methods would break unless updated, but no such updates are shown.

aspect_3_judge.summary: This refactoring is purely cosmetic, renaming methods without addressing the interface segregation violation. The fat interface remains intact with all four abstract methods still forcing DataArray and Dataset to implement role-inappropriate methods. The more generic names obscure rather than fix the segregation problem, and critical cross-file updates to DataArray, Dataset, and the strategy registry are missing, suggesting the refactoring would break the codebase.
